notes:
# Pick several, act on all of them {check_circle}
A Select button above the meeting list turns every row into a tick box. Choose
a few, or all of them, and the footer moves them into a folder or deletes them
in one go — with one question asked once, rather than once per meeting.

# A new meeting is not a meeting until you save it {plus}
Pressing New used to create the meeting there and then, armed, with no link in
it. It now opens a blank form with a draft row at the top of the list, and
writes nothing until you press Save changes. Nothing is left behind if you
change your mind.

# Search time zones the way you say them {globe}
EST, PST, CST and the rest now find the zones that go by those names — all of
them, not one each. So do cities the database has never heard of: Boston, San
Francisco, Seattle, Bali, Penang, Beijing, Mumbai. Each result says why it is
in the list.

# Light or dark, whichever you prefer {sliders}
Settings › General now carries a Theme switch: follow the Mac, or hold
RecordLah in one or the other. It takes effect when the app reopens, and there
is a button there to do that straight away.

# The footer says what is coming next {clock}
Instead of "All systems ready", the line along the bottom names the next
recording that will actually happen, and when. A meeting with no link is never
promised.

---

Everything else in this release:

**Deleting**

- Deleting asks one clear question, with what happens to the recordings spelled
  out on its own line and the number of meetings named on the button.
- A delete writes the meeting list to disk BEFORE it moves any file to the
  Trash, so an interruption can never leave a meeting pointing at a recording
  that is no longer there.
- Deleting a meeting no longer freezes the window.

**Duplicating**

- "Create another" is now called Duplicate — it is the same action as the one
  in the row's menu, and it now says so.
- A duplicate keeps everything except the date, which is the one field that is
  certainly wrong when you are scheduling something again. It lands at the top
  of the list and the form opens on the next free slot.
- The copy is scrolled into view, wherever the list happened to be.

**Menus and panels**

- Every menu in the app is now RecordLah's own panel rather than a system one.
  The system ones left the window's mouse tracking stale behind them: the next
  click anywhere was swallowed, and the control under the pointer showed the
  wrong cursor until it landed.
- Escape closes every panel, menu, picker and dialog — including the ones with
  nothing to type in, which ignored it before.
- Scrolling closes the row's menu instead of leaving it floating over a list
  that has moved on.

**Scrolling**

- The wheel and the trackpad scroll whatever is under the pointer. Opening a
  row's menu used to send every scroll to the pane on the right, however far
  away the pointer was, until you clicked the list again.

**Notes**

- Diagrams in the notes keep their shape: fenced blocks are set in a monospace
  face instead of being re-flowed as prose.
- Your own question sits against the right-hand edge at any window width, and
  the reply's bubble is drawn the size it actually is.
- Copy says what it copied, in the notes window rather than in the window
  behind it.

**Appearance**

- Cards in the meeting form, in Settings and on the Invitations tab are rounded
  and have lost their hard outlines.
- The selected item in the sidebar is a rounded pill, like every other selected
  thing in the app.
- On a narrow window the schedule lays itself out properly: Repeats beside its
  label, Date and Time paired, the time zone across the full width — and the
  day shortcuts drop to their own line instead of running off the edge.
- The folder icon is drawn as a folder with a real tab, and the count pills sit
  clear of the scrollbar.

**Fixes**

- The update check no longer leaves "Checking for updates…" on screen for the
  rest of the session.
- The Analysis and Resources cards on a finished recording are laid out
  correctly again.
